text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SEV2 - sustained p99 latency breach for streaming.generate (SLO: p99 < 600ms). Current window 30m, p99 ~2.8s, p95 ~1.2s. Customers flagged: AcmeCorp (prod), BetaApps (prod). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/streams/alerts/2311112222 :rotating_light:

maria: oncall acked — i'm taking lead. paging hardware + infra. i'm collecting traces and checking node health. tagging @sre_ash and @eng-tim.

sre_ash: on it. can you paste p95/p99 numbers and which region/zone?

maria: p95=1200ms, p99=2800ms across streaming region-us-east-1b. tail looks like long stalls for streaming sessions that rely on kv-cache warmups.

eng-tim: looking at runtime metrics now — seeing repeated long stalls on a handful of accelerator hosts. nvidia-smi snapshot from host accel-48: 

```
GPU 2: Temp 94C, PWR 250W, SM 98%, ECC errs: correctable=432, uncorrectable=0
Clocks: 1575 MHz
Throttle reason: GPU_TEMP_LIMIT, BOARD_POWER
NVML_THROTTLING: Active
```

eng-tim: also seeing streaming stalls where token generation stalls for 800-1500ms per chunk when requests hit that host. KV cache miss rates spiked when those hosts went into thermal throttle and started dropping CUDA clocks.

support-jade: customer report from AcmeCorp at 12:07: "streaming freezes for ~2s, then resumes; user experience is jittery" — they're seeing impact in their prod. raised a support ticket.

kevin: immediate mitigation options: 1) route traffic away from the affected node pool (scale and migrate), 2) switch to a lower-compute variant/model for streaming (faster CPU path), 3) temporarily bump routing to dedicated fallback pool. which do we want to execute now?

maria: let's do 1 + 2 in parallel. ops-lin — can you cordon and drain accel-48 then trigger autoscaler to replace nodes? eng-tim — prepare the lower-compute variant rollout (no config change in client) and toggle routing weight. i'll coordinate customer comms.

ops-lin: running commands now:

```bash
kubectl cordon node/accel-48 -n inference
kubectl drain node/accel-48 -n inference --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# scale up fallback pool
kubectl scale deploy inference-fallback-pool --replicas=6 -n inference
```

ops-lin: cordon succeeded, drain in progress — evicting ~24 streaming pods. some sessions will reconnect; routing should shift.

eng-tim: posting temporary routing override to shift 60% of streaming traffic to fallback variant (low-latency-quant). rollout command: 

```json
{"route":"/v1/streams/generate","weights":{"default":40,"low-latency-quant":60}}
```

eng-tim: also kicking off soft-restart of runtime on accel-48 to flush stale CUDA contexts (if drain doesn't complete). note: ECC correctable counts are high; hardware team should inspect.

sre_ash: also enabling short-term prefix caching to reduce backend load: cache TTL 60s for hot prefixes. patch applied.

incident-bot: Paging hardware-team @hardware-oncall at 12:22. Conference bridge created: https://meet.redwood/example/incident-2311112222.

ops-lin: drain completed. node accel-48 is cordoned and pods evicted. autoscaler scaled fallback pool to 6 replicas.

kevin: early metrics after routing shift: p95 down to 850ms, p99 down to 1.1s in the last 5m. still above SLO but trending. posting smoothed times: 

- before mitigation (12:00-12:20): p95 1200ms, p99 2800ms
- after mitigation (12:25-12:30): p95 850ms, p99 1100ms

support-jade: customer update posted: "we're aware of streaming latency spikes; mitigation in progress; will follow up when resolved."

eng-tim: log snippet from runtime on accel-48 just before drain: 

```
[2025-10-03T12:18:33Z] stream_worker.cc: generate_chunk(453) stall detected: 1243ms token stall, reason=nvml_throttle (GPU_TEMP_LIMIT)
[2025-10-03T12:19:01Z] nvml: ecc_correctables=432 -> increasing trend
[2025-10-03T12:19:01Z] kv_cache: miss_rate spike 0.63 -> 0.88
```

maria: hardware-oncall joined bridge. hardware says likely thermal throttling + high correctable ECC rate on accel-48. recommend RMA/replace chassis after-hours.

sre_ash: for short-term we should keep fallback routing active for 2 hours and monitor p99; if stable we can de-escalate to SEV3. also propose enabling session-level sticky fallback for affected customer to avoid reconnect flapping.

eng-tim: creating follow-up ticket to replace accel-48 and to run a soak test across the replacement pool. ticket: https://tickets.redwood/INC-23111122.

ops-lin: confirmed: accel-48 marked OOS and scheduled for replacement next maintenance window (2025-10-04 02:00 UTC).

kevin: after 30m of fallback routing p95=730ms p99=920ms — within SLAs for most customers but AcmeCorp reported occasional micro-jitters. recommending full postmortem and model-routing rules to avoid single-node hot spots.

support-jade: AcmeCorp acknowledged the update and asked for root cause summary once available.

maria: incident status -> mitigated. customer impact: AcmeCorp and BetaApps saw intermittent 1-3s stalls between 12:07-12:25 UTC, ~2% of requests from those tenants affected. mitigation actions: cordon+drain accel-48, reroute 60% traffic to low-latency variant, scale fallback pool, enable short TTL prefix cache. follow-ups: hardware RMA, postmortem, routing hardening.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to MONITORING at 12:48. SEV status updated to SEV3.

maria: thanks team. i'll start the postmortem doc and notify growth/pg teams. please drop any remaining notes in the doc. closing channel updates here. :white_check_mark:
